The Azerbaijani Army launched a counter-offensive operation, later called the "Iron Fist", on September 27, 2020, in response to the large-scale provocation of the Armenian armed forces along the frontline. The 44-day Second Karabakh War ended with the liberation of Azerbaijan’s territories from nearly 30-year Armenian occupation and the restoration of territorial integrity. President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev was interviewed by Russian Interfax agency. Trend presents the interview: - Thank you, Mr. President, for finding the time for an interview with our agency despite your busy schedule. It was exactly one month yesterday since the counter- offensive of the Azerbaijani Armed Forces began in Nagorno- Karabakh. How would you assess this month from the point of view of the military- political settlement of the conflict? - The Azerbaijani army has demonstrated its advantage on the battlefield. Significant parts of the occupied territories have been liberated in one month. Given that the Armenian side had been building fortifications in the occupied lands for almost 30 years, there were several lines of defense. Also, the terrain itself is more favorable for the Armenian side. It is mountainous and our servicemen had to overcome both engineering fortifications and mountainous terrain when carrying out the counterattack. Despite all these factors, significant territories in the occupied lands of our country have been liberated in one month, and this shows that the Azerbaijani army is considered one of the most combat- effective armies in the world for a reason. According to the rankings periodically published by organizations that assess the military potential of countries, the Azerbaijani army is among top 50 armies in the world. The professionalism, training, combat effectiveness and, most importantly, fighting morale have certainly contributed to our success in many respects. And, of course, the equipment available to the Azerbaijani army. We have liberated the cities of Fuzuli, Jabrayil, Zangilan, Gubadli, a part of Khojavand district. The successful mission, the successful advance of the Azerbaijani army continues. I have said several times during this month that we want the settlement of the conflict to move from a military to a political phase. But, unfortunately, the Armenian side has grossly violated the ceasefire regime for the third time, attempted to re- occupy the territories we have liberated, and is pushing for a continuation of the confrontation. Therefore, I am answering your question again: the military- political settlement is the only possible way. We would like the military phase to end and issues of further de- occupation of Azerbaijani territories to be resolved at the negotiating table. - Mr. President, you noted that Baku is interested in completing the military phase as quickly as possible. How long do you think it can last at the present time and is Baku ready to be content with seven districts around Nagorno- Karabakh? - I have repeatedly said in my appeals to the Azerbaijani people and in numerous interviews this month that we are ready to stop at any moment, even today. But for this to happen, the Armenian side must commit to withdrawing its troops from the rest of the occupied territories. Therefore, I cannot predict how long the military confrontation will last. It depends on the Armenian side. As I said, their constant attempts to recapture our lands have failed. I think this should already be enough for them to understand that they will not achieve anything by military means. Unfortunately, on the political plane they are demonstrating a non- constructive approach, as I said, and have grossly violated the ceasefire three times. Based on this, of course, we will continue to plan on further action. As for the occupied territories, of course, the Azerbaijanis must return to all the occupied territories where they used to live, and this has always been my approach. First of all, these are Shusha, Khankandi and other lands that have been inhabited by Azerbaijanis for centuries. I also said that our vision for a settlement lies in the co- existence of the Armenian and Azerbaijani population of Nagorno- Karabakh. It so happened historically that the Armenian population has been living on these lands for 200 years. We all know the history of the resettlement of Armenians from Eastern Anatolia and Iran. But it so happened. They have lived there for 200 years. And we have no objection to the continued presence of the Armenian population. On the contrary, I have always said that thousands of citizens of Armenian nationality live in Azerbaijan, that Armenians and Azerbaijanis live together in neighboring countries and get along quite well. Why can't this be achieved in Nagorno- Karabakh? Our vision is this: Azerbaijanis should return to all the territories they lived in. The Armenian population should also live on this land. And in the conditions of good neighborliness, we will strive to heal the wounds of war. - So it means that Baku will not stop until Armenian servicemen withdraw from all the occupied territories. - We need the Armenian side in the person of its leadership to undertake a commitment to withdraw troops from the occupied territories. We haven't heard that yet. And provided that the Armenian side also stops it because all three violations of the ceasefire were committed by the Armenian side. So this is a flagrant violation of the ceasefire, which was agreed in Washington. Prior to that, the ceasefire agreed in Moscow was violated by the Armenian side the next day when they launched a ballistic missile from the territory of Armenia to Ganja. https://www.ng.ru/cis/2026-10-27/5_9612_.body: Конституционный суд отказался допрашивать премьер-министра Ираклия Кобахидзе, как того требовала оппозиция. Фото Reuters Грузинская оппозиция решила, что уличные протесты – единственный способ заставить Конституционный суд (КС) не запрещать «Единое национальное движение» (ЕНД), Коалицию за перемены, «Лело – Сильную Грузию», «Гахарию за Грузию» и «Федералистов». С конца октября в центре Тбилиси они будут проводить массовые митинги под общим лозунгом «Грузия без Иванишвили». «Эта акция – начало новой волны, а не начало протеста. Она называется «Грузия без Иванишвили». Грузия действительно заслуживает лучшего, и мы действительно движемся в Европу. Но у нас ничего не получится, пока Бидзина Иванишвили (основатель «Грузинской мечты») остается в Грузии человеком, узурпировавшим власть», – заявил один из лидеров «Коалиции за перемены» Ника Гварамия. По его словам, кульминация борьбы должна состояться 28 ноября – в этот день в 2024-м правительство «Грузинской мечты» решило приостановить переговоры о евроинтеграции. Правда, пока в протестах участвуют всего несколько тысяч человек. «Сами по себе протесты не смогут ни на что повлиять, но они напоминают «Грузинской мечте», что запрет организаций не приведет к исчезновению ее противников. Даже если их запретят до 28 ноября, что вполне возможно, их члены станут диссидентами, а протесты будут организовывать другие гражданские активисты. Правда, оппозиционерам все еще нужно придумать что-то кроме критики Иванишвили, потому что грузины ждут, когда им предложат альтернативу нынешнему режиму, а не причину, по которой его нужно не любить... Конечно, при желании можно запретить свыше 30% граждан Грузии, которые так или иначе связали себя с опальными партиями, в том числе голосуя за них, но это уже другая история», – считает профессор Черноморского международного университета Ника Читадзе. Тем временем КС отказался допрашивать Бидзину Иванишвили, премьер-министра Ираклия Кобахидзе, мэра Каху Каладзе и других лидеров правящей партии. Суд настаивает, что на процессе не должно быть политических заявлений. В том числе оппозиционерам запретили говорить о том, что основатель «Грузинской мечты» сам был агентом ЕС, так как с 2010 по 2011 год имел французский паспорт. При этом представитель «Гахарии за Грузию» Гига Парулава рассказал журналистам, что, как только КС признает его партию неконституционной, она будет распущена и ее депутатам придется отказаться от мандатов. В этом случае в заксобрании останутся только «Грузинская мечта», которая контролирует правительство с 2012-го, и ее партнер «Сила народа», чей представитель Михаил Кавелашвили стал президентом в 2024-м. Как известно, иск «Грузинской мечты» основан на двух ключевых тезисах. Во-первых, ЕНД виновна в начале войны 2008 года, поставила под угрозу территориальную целостность страны и грузинские национальные интересы, желая выслужиться перед Западом. Причем в этом обвиняют не только партию Михаила Саакашвили, но и «Коалицию за перемены» и «Федералистов», которые откололись от нее несколько лет назад. «Гахария за Грузию» и «Лело» никак не связаны с Саакашвили и не могут быть причастны к той войне, поэтому для них подготовили другое основание: в 2024-м все обвиняемые, кроме «Федералистов», появившихся позже, подписали соглашение о совместной борьбе с «Грузинской мечтой». Партия власти расценивает это как совместную подготовку к госперевороту. Примечательно, что «Грузинскую хартию» подготовила тогда еще президент Саломе Зурабишвили, которую пока ни в чем не обвиняют. Всего под документом подписались не меньше 17 организаций. Зурабишвили надеялась с его помощью объединить вообще всю оппозицию накануне парламентских выборов и таким образом возглавить ее. «В действительности мы имеем дело с Коллективным национальным движением, будь то «родная» или «родительская» партия, находящаяся у власти с 2003 года. Если проанализировать содержание даже деклараций, совместно подписанных партиями Коллективного национального движения, то, конечно же, это очень четкое и недвусмысленное подтверждение того, что они заранее заявили о готовности к сотрудничеству, даже в составе правительства, и к совместной работе над формированием правительства в преддверии парламентских выборов 2024 года. Повторюсь еще раз, в парламентской республике очень сложно найти более ясное выражение того, что конкретные политические партии представляют одни и те же цели, по сути, одну и ту же идеологию», – говорит член «Грузинской мечты» Торнике Чейшвили. Однако сторонники оппозиции настаивают, что для запрета партий команда Иванишвили должна доказать не их сотрудничество друг с другом, а злой умысел, о котором говорится в 23 статье Конституции. «Если нет цели свержения и насильственного изменения конституционного порядка, посягательства на независимость страны и нарушения территориальной целостности, никого запрещать нельзя», – уверена экс-прокурор и судья Мая Мцариашвили.

В феврале 2020 года президент Г.Бердымухамедов распорядился возвести 300-метровый монумент к 30-летию независимости, который отмечался 27 сентября 2021 года. Но построен он не был и о данном проекте больше не упоминается. Существующий монумент независимости (на фото) был возведен в 2001 году. https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-russia-s.body: News Russian Strikes Hit Kyiv As Oleshky Cease-Fire Takes Effect By RFE/RL's Ukrainian Service October 27, 2026 01:54 CET Updated October 27, 2026 09:43 CET Russian Strikes Hit Kyiv As Oleshky Cease-Fire Takes Effect Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Ukrainian soldiers prepare food parcels for the residents of Oleshky. (file photo) The US-negotiated cease-fire aimed at allowing humanitarian aid into the southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky took effect in the early hours of October 27, shortly after Russian air attacks struck Kyiv, hitting a university dormitory and other civilian sites and killing at least one person. The start of the cease-fire, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump last week and confirmed by Moscow and Kyiv, comes amid what she described as a dire situation in Oleshky, a frontline city on the brink of disaster, where the remaining population consists primarily of elderly residents urgently in need of medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water. SEE ALSO: White House Says Melania Trump Brokers Localized Cease-Fire For Occupied Ukrainian City "The cease-fire has begun, and the Ukrainian side is honoring its commitments," Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, wrote on Telegram on October 27. "Today, at 3:00 a.m. Kyiv time and 4:00 a.m. Moscow time, a cease-fire was introduced in designated areas associated with the humanitarian mission," he added. The Russian Defense Ministry said it had halted fire in the Kherson direction and introduced a "cease-fire regime" ahead of a planned humanitarian operation in Oleshky. Oleshky lies on the Russian-occupied bank of the Dnieper River, opposite the regional capital of Kherson. Before Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022, the city had approximately 24,000 residents. Melania Trump's office estimates that between 1,700 and 2,000 people remain, including about 50 children. Most are believed to be elderly residents who have been unable or unwilling to leave. There has been no formal demographic count since 2022. The destruction of the nearby Kakhovka Dam in June 2023 compounded the devastation, with an estimated 90 percent of Oleshky's territory flooded. Russian Strikes Hit Kyiv As Zelenskyy Seeks Air Defenses Russian air attacks struck Kyiv late on October 26, hitting a university dormitory and other civilian sites and killing at least one person. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called on Ukraine's partners to provide the "proper tools" for the country to defend itself. Russian forces launched 16 ballistic missiles and 280 drones at Ukraine overnight, Zelenskyy said on October 27, while the Ukrainian Air Force reported that Ukrainian air defenses had shot down or intercepted two ballistic missiles and 255 drones. Locator map: Oleshky, Kherson Region "Russia is constantly taking new steps toward escalation," the Ukrainian leader said. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said at least 14 people were injured in the strikes, "most of whom were students from a university dormitory." Klitschko also reported that a Russian strike damaged a major bridge spanning the Dnieper River in Kyiv. "Experts are assessing the extent of the damage to the Southern Bridge. Traffic across the bridge is currently closed," he wrote on Telegram. "It is precisely under such circumstances, when the threat is constant, when strikes can come at any moment and target cities and villages directly, that artificial delays in providing air defense to Ukraine help terror," Zelenskyy said in a post on social media . "It is important that our partners understand that Ukraine needs the proper tools to destroy Russian ballistic missile launchers. This would be the most effective way to save lives. It is important that the world sees that Russia is showing nothing but a desire to kill and continue waging war. " In its latest report issued on October 26, the UN's Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine said that the Russian authorities had committed war crimes and crimes against humanity by attacking civilians and critical energy infrastructure, among other violations of international law. US lawmakers have been challenging President Donald Trump's decision to ease restrictions on Russian energy imports and demanding guarantees that Kyiv will retain access to critical American military and intelligence support. In a series of legislative initiatives, congressional inquiries, and appeals to the administration, Republicans and Democrats have warned that decisions benefiting Moscow or disrupting Ukraine’s battlefield capabilities could undermine US national security, weaken congressional authority, and prolong Russia’s war. The pushback comes after the administration authorized transactions involving Russian diesel fuel, amid reports that Ukraine’s access to SpaceX’s Starlink and military-grade Starshield satellite communications systems had been restricted. SEE ALSO: Bipartisan US Lawmakers Push Back On Trump's Russia Policy, Vow Support For Ukraine Ukrainian officials say the disruptions have affected military operations, although they have said in recent days that satellite connection speeds had been restored. Questions remain about who imposed the restrictions. For several months, Zelenskyy has also called on the US and other allies to step up supplies of critical defense systems such as Patriot missiles amid almost nightly barrages of Russian ballistic missiles and drones. He said last week that Ukraine was still waiting for previously agreed deliveries of interceptors for Patriot air-defense systems. Despite overwhelming evidence to the contrary, Russian officials deny targeting civilian infrastructure in the conflict, which has raged since the Kremlin launched its full-scale invasion of its neighbor in February 2022. The university hit in the attack was identified as the State University of Trade and Economics (SUTE), one of Kyiv's largest schools with more than 15,000 students. https://www.rferl.org/a/tensions-mecca-a.body: News Iran, Regional Countries Agree To Continue Talks After Tehran Meeting By Daud Khattak October 26, 2026 14:43 CET Updated October 26, 2026 19:10 CET Iran, Regional Countries Agree To Continue Talks After Tehran Meeting Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Houthis hold their weapons as they rally in solidarity with Iran and Lebanon, amid the US-Israeli war with Iran, in the Yemeni capital Sanaa on March 27. Iran and three members of a regional mutual-defense pact have agreed to continue talks after their first meeting in Tehran, Iranian state television reported. Iranian officials met with representatives of Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey, the signatories to the Mecca Defense Alliance on October 26, to defuse tensions in the region. The sides “agreed to continue discussions to strengthen cooperation...including on regional peace and security,” state television said. The meeting came as the US-Iran war and increasing attacks by Iran-aligned Houthi rebels on Saudi Arabia have left the region reeling and are impacting global flows of oil and other cargo. 'Last-Ditch Effort' Ahead of the meeting, a senior security official in Islamabad told RFE/RL that one of the main points of the meeting was to try to convince Iran to use its influence over Houthis to stop attacks on Saudi Arabia. The official said the alliance countries were prepared to raise the prospect of closer Saudi-Israeli security cooperation as leverage. “The key question is why Iran should comply? The answer is that Saudi Arabia may ask for support from Israel and that will potentially require them to join the Abraham Accords,” said the official. The accords, signed in 2020, normalized relations between Israel and several Arab states, including the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain. “Since Turkey has already diplomatic relations with Israel, the trio might place this scenario on the table should Tehran refuse to rein in the Houthis,” said the official. While Iran may comply by using its influence over the Houthis, the official added that it is unlikely that the regime would soften its stance on negotiations with the United States over the war. Islamabad-based analyst Azaz Syed said the US-Iran conflict would be just as important during the meeting amid fears Washington is preparing to renew its military attacks on Iran. Pakistan's powerful army chief, Asim Munir, was in Tehran last week where he reportedly delivered a "last warning" to the Iranian government. “Apparently, this was a last-ditch effort to convince the Iranians” to come to a negotiated settlement with the United States, Syed told RFE/RL. “The three partners will ask for an end to Houthi attacks, of course, but the key message is the broader settlement.” Hamidreza Azizi, senior analyst at the Belgium-based International Crisis Group, said that the meeting in Tehran was a last-minute attempt to prevent another escalation. “The immediate priority seems to be finding a way to prevent the resumption of war between Iran and the United States,” Azizi told RFERL. Azizi said the October 26 meeting was essentially a continuation of diplomatic efforts already under way, and the timing suggests that regional countries are increasingly concerned that these efforts may be running out of time. The Houthis, allies of Tehran who primarily operate from Yemen, have intensified their missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, targeting airports and oil infrastructure at a time when energy transit in the Middle East has already been curtailed by the closing of the Strait of Hormuz, the waterway that normally sees around one-fifth of the world's oil and gas flows transported through it. Earlier this month, Houthi rebels attacked Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport, killing 13 people and wounding more than 300. The rebels have also warned airlines against using Saudi airspace. Saudi Arabia has in turn launched strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen. The conflicts have shed light on the complex diplomatic relations between nations across the Middle and Near East. The Mecca Alliance enshrines a collective security arrangement modeled on NATO's Article 5, stating that "any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all." Iran-Pakistan Tensions The meeting also came amid already heightened tensions between Iran and Pakistan after Islamabad closed two border crossings between its Balochistan Province and Iran’s Sistan-Baluchistan Province. Pakistan has also introduced changes in its E-form procedure, a digital declaration authorizing the tracking of foreign currency remittances, for Iranian exports coming into the country. Sources say Islamabad has also suspended operating clearance for Mahan Air, the Iranian airline believed to have links with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC). Iranian and Pakistani authorities have neither admitted nor denied the reports. The Iranian side, in reaction, stopped the export of Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG) to Pakistan causing manifold increase in gas prices for domestic and commercial consumers. Pakistan imports around 7,000 metric tons of LPG every day from Iran. "The visit also underscores the pivotal role of the Mecca Pact states in fostering regional security and stability, and their commitment to working with all nations in the region toward achieving this goal," said Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly in a social media post . Commenting on the closure of Iran-Pakistan border crossings, Tehran envoy to Islamabad Reza Amiri Moghadam said in a social media post that consultations with the Pakistani side are under way to address the issue of cross-border trade. Moghadam said several hundred trucks carrying LPG have crossed the Rimdan border into Gabd on the Pakistani side. However, despite having remained there for several weeks, these trucks have yet to be unloaded or cleared up, further complicating the movement of goods and the smooth flow of bilateral trade. Significant Step Rabia Akhtar, a professor of international relations at the University of Lahore, said the immediate concern among the three partners was to prevent the current confrontation from escalating further. “Nobody at that table really benefits from another regional war,” Akhtar told RFE/RL, who added that if the participants can establish some understanding on restraint -- particularly regarding Saudi security, the Houthis, and further escalation with Iran -- that would already be a meaningful outcome. “So I would see this as an attempt at regional crisis management rather than the birth of a new security architecture. And in the present circumstances, even that would be quite consequential,” Akhtar said. Azizi of the International Crisis Group said the meeting could help reduce tensions, at least temporarily, by keeping channels of communication open. “But the main problem remains unresolved: Iran wants credible security guarantees against renewed attacks, while the regional mediators have limited ability to influence Washington's decisions.” Iran, Regional Countries Agree To Continue Talks After Tehran Meeting Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Follow us Facebook X (Twitter) Youtube Instagram Follow us Print Daud Khattak Daud Khattak is a senior international correspondent covering the Near East in RFE/RL’s Central Newsroom. He was previously the managing editor of RFE/RL's Radio Mashaal. This item is part of News Iran

https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-and-iran-.body: Iran Russia And Iran Expand Nuclear Cooperation As International Oversight Weakens By Aleksandr Dubrovsky October 26, 2026 17:24 CET Russia And Iran Expand Nuclear Cooperation As International Oversight Weakens Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google The Bushehr nuclear power plant is the centerpiece of Iranian-Russian nuclear cooperation. Russia and Iran are expanding their nuclear cooperation as both countries face Western sanctions and international isolation. Their partnership includes the construction of nuclear power plants, fuel supplies, and broader technological cooperation. While Bushehr, Iran’s first operating nuclear power station, has long been the centerpiece of their relationship, Moscow and Tehran are planning new nuclear facilities and cooperation in other areas of technology, raising questions about the ability of international agencies to monitor Iran’s nuclear activities. Russia’s state nuclear corporation Rosatom has played a key role in completing and operating Bushehr, on Iran’s southern coast. A contract to complete the plant’s first reactor was signed in 1995, but the unit did not begin full commercial electricity generation until 2013. Rosatom has continued work at the site despite the military escalation in the Middle East. After the start of the US-Iran war in February, Rosatom evacuated most of its workers from Iran. But many of the personnel have since returned; by October 11, the Russian nuclear body reported that 135 engineering and technical specialists were back working at the site. Construction is also continuing on two additional reactor units at Bushehr. Work on a second unit has progressed beyond 60 percent completion, with a target of starting operations in 2029, while construction of a third unit is also under way, according to Rosatom. Who Benefits Most From The Cooperation? The Bushehr plant has taken on broader strategic significance as Moscow and Tehran deepen their relationship. The legal foundation of this cooperation is the two countries' Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty, which officially entered into force in October 2025. The practical road map, however, is the intergovernmental Cooperation Plan For 2024–2026, which was approved in September 2024. For Russia, the nuclear partnership provides commercial opportunities and a way to maintain influence in the Middle East. For Iran, Russian assistance offers access to nuclear technology, expertise, and fuel supplies. SEE ALSO: With War In Limbo, Influential Iranian Officials Openly Call For A Nuclear Bomb The benefits are not necessarily equal, though. In a November 2025 article for the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, analyst Nikita Smagin wrote that “the balance in the relationship is once again shifting in Russia’s favor." Iran is in dire need of investment, and "Russia remains one of the few available sources," Smagin wrote. Analysts at Israel’s Institute for National Security Studies (INSS) have argued that Russia increasingly views cooperation with Iran as a way to strengthen its position in negotiations with Washington. In a June analysis, INSS researchers Dmitry Kovchegin and Arkady Mil-Man described Moscow’s policy toward Iran’s nuclear program as a “calculated balancing strategy.” "[Russia's policy comprises] rhetorical condemnation of military escalation, particularly strikes against nuclear facilities; the provision of limited assistance that does not affect the balance of power between the parties to the conflict; and the offering of mediation services, while seeking to improve its relations with the United States," the authors wrote. New Nuclear Power Plant The nuclear partnership is not limited to Bushehr. In September 2025, Russia and Iran signed an agreement for the construction of a new nuclear power plant, Sirik, in Iran’s southern Hormozgan Province, near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran’s state news agency, IRNA, reported that the deal was worth $25 billion and that the units would have a combined capacity of about 5 gigawatts. (By comparison, the finished Bushehr complex would have a capacity of under 3 gigawatts.) If completed, Sirik would further tie Iran’s civilian nuclear energy sector to Russian technology and fuel supplies for decades. SEE ALSO: 'Russia Is Behaving Like A Rogue State': Historian Margaret MacMillan On The Risk Of A Wider Global Conflict Russia and Iran have strengthened their political, economic and military ties in recent years, with Western sanctions encouraging both countries to develop alternative channels for trade and technological cooperation. A 2025 analysis by the US-based Center for Naval Analyses (CNA) found that Russia and Iran had expanded military contacts, arms transfers, and technical cooperation since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The two countries have also pursued new trade agreements, closer links between their banking sectors, increased cross-border trade, and investment in strategic sectors. However, the CNA researchers pointed out that competition between the two economies could constrain the longer-term growth of their economic relationship. Monitoring Concerns This burgeoning Russian-Iranian cooperation, especially in the nuclear sphere, comes as the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) faces major obstacles in monitoring Iran’s nuclear activities. In a report published on June 4, the agency said it had conducted an inspection at Bushehr on June 1–3 but had not been able to carry out inspections during the reporting period at other declared nuclear sites, the most sensitive of which are four uranium enrichment facilities. The IAEA also said it could not verify the status of nuclear material at those sites or confirm whether Iran had suspended uranium enrichment, reprocessing of spent reactor fuel, and heavy-water-related activities -- processes that can support the production of nuclear weapons -- as required by relevant UN Security Council and IAEA resolutions. The report highlighted a significant gap in international oversight, but its findings describe the situation during the reporting period and should not be taken as a real-time assessment of access to Iranian facilities today. Russia faces extensive Western sanctions imposed after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. The measures target key sectors of its economy, including energy, finance, trade, and defense, and are intended to limit Moscow’s ability to finance the war and access technology used by its military. Russia has also faced sanctions over human rights abuses and actions viewed by Western governments as threats to international security. Iran has faced decades of US and international sanctions over its nuclear program, concerns about possible nuclear weapons development, and its support for armed groups across the Middle East. Additional restrictions target Iran’s ballistic missile program, military activities, and human rights abuses. Sanctions were tightened further in recent years amid growing concerns over Iran’s nuclear activities and its military cooperation with Russia, including Tehran's supply of drones used in Russia’s war against Ukraine. The expansion of nuclear projects alongside reduced international oversight has prompted concerns among nonproliferation specialists about transparency and the potential for sensitive technologies to be diverted. Some analysts have argued that Russia’s civilian nuclear cooperation with Iran could have consequences beyond electricity generation, namely Iran’s accumulation of uranium enriched to 60 percent. Uranium enriched to that level is not weapons-grade, but it can be enriched further to around 90 percent, the level generally associated with nuclear weapons. https://www.rferl.org/a/amid-legal-uncer.body: Russia Amid Legal Uncertainty, US Lawmakers Warn Banks, Ports Over Russian Diesel Imports By Alex Raufoglu October 27, 2026 12:06 CET Amid Legal Uncertainty, US Lawmakers Warn Banks, Ports Over Russian Diesel Imports Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Under the arrangement with President Trump, Moscow would supply hundreds of thousands of metric tons of diesel to the United States. WASHINGTON -- A bipartisan group of US lawmakers have warned American banks, port authorities, and fuel-industry groups against facilitating imports of Russian diesel, raising the prospect of congressional investigations and legal action over President Donald Trump’s decision to ease restrictions on Russian fuel. In letters sent to the chief executives of major US banks and the heads of several port authorities, the lawmakers warned that importing Russian diesel could violate federal law and expose companies to civil and criminal liability. They also said the imports would raise national-security concerns by providing Moscow with revenue to help finance its war against Ukraine. SEE ALSO: Trump Makes Deal With Putin On Diesel Exports. Ukraine Calls It A 'Gift' The intervention comes after Trump recently announced an arrangement with Russian President Vladimir Putin under which Moscow would supply hundreds of thousands of metric tons of diesel to the United States, with additional shipments planned in the coming months. The US Treasury Department subsequently issued General License 135, granting a six-month exemption from certain sanctions restrictions. The letters signal a potential new front in the political and legal battle over the administration’s Russia policy. Democrats could gain significant investigative powers if they regain control of one or both chambers of Congress in the November midterm elections. “Any importation of Russian diesel into the US raises significant legal questions and may be subject to legal action, as well as congressional investigations,” the lawmakers wrote. The group includes Democratic Senators Jeanne Shaheen, Ron Wyden, Sheldon Whitehouse, Chris Coons and Elizabeth Warren, as well as outgoing Republican Senator Thom Tillis and Representative Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee. They urged companies not to facilitate the purchase, transportation, importation, unloading, storage, financing, or distribution of Russian-origin diesel until the relevant legal requirements had been met. The lawmakers also demanded that the companies preserve records of proposed or completed transactions, including contracts, shipping documents, payment records, port reservations and communications with suppliers and US government officials dating back to September 1. Recipients were asked to confirm by October 28 that they had implemented the required preservation measures and to disclose whether they had knowledge of any proposed or actual Russian diesel imports. The letters went to the chief executives of major US banks, including Goldman Sachs , as well as the port authorities of Houston, Corpus Christi and Beaumont in Texas and New York/New Jersey. SEE ALSO: Bipartisan US Lawmakers Push Back On Trump's Russia Policy, Vow Support For Ukraine Public reporting and vessel-tracking data cited by the lawmakers indicate that ships carrying Russian diesel could arrive at Beaumont and New York/New Jersey as early as the end of October. At the center of the dispute is whether the administration’s licensing action is consistent with restrictions established by Congress. The lawmakers cited the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act of 2022, which generally prohibits imports of Russian-origin energy products unless the president certifies to Congress, following a period of consultation, that Russia has ceased military hostilities in Ukraine, poses no immediate military threat to NATO members, and recognizes Ukrainians’ right to choose their government. They also argued that Section 216 of the Countering America’s Adversaries Through Sanctions Act requires congressional review before certain licensing actions that significantly alter US foreign policy toward Russia. The lawmakers said the administration had not fulfilled that requirement. The administration maintains that its action is lawful and consistent with previous decisions by the Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control, which administers US sanctions. SEE ALSO: Former US Diplomat Fried Warns Mixed Signals Could Undercut Russia Sanctions The White House dismissed the lawmakers’ initiative as politically motivated. “The Democrats are already telegraphing that, once again, they have no agenda to improve the lives of Americans and will instead continue their decade-long obsession with investigating President Trump,” spokesperson Taylor Rogers said. The letters do not establish that any company has committed a crime. Instead, they warn that participating in the transactions could expose companies to legal challenges and investigations despite the administration’s assurances that the waiver is valid. Representative Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, separately warned major fuel-industry associations that companies importing Russian diesel could face civil and criminal penalties, including up to 20 years in prison. Raskin argued that Trump’s move could not override statutory prohibitions and warned that companies could be held accountable “whether in this administration -- or the next.” Experts say the warnings could complicate the administration’s plans even if the waiver reduces the risk of sanctions violations under US executive-branch rules. Michael Wain, a senior international trade policy adviser at the law firm Akin, told RFE/RL that the congressional pushback was noteworthy but that US imports represented only part of the picture. “General License 135 covers a broad range of Russian diesel transactions and substantially reduces US sanctions risk for foreign firms that stay within its terms,” Wain said. However, he added, companies must still consider British, European Union and other jurisdictions’ sanctions rules. SEE ALSO: Kasparov Says Talks With Putin Pointless, War Is 'Ideological Basis' Of His Rule A key question, he said, is whether foreign buyers previously reluctant to handle Russian fuel will now feel more comfortable doing so -- an outcome that may be part of the administration’s objective. Glen Howard, president of the Saratoga Foundation and a longtime Russia strategist, said the letters could make major US banks reluctant to finance the transactions. “It is very significant because it was sent to each of the major US banks and will likely cause them to freeze in place any efforts by the Trump administration to proceed with the sale,” Howard told RFE/RL. He said the move suggested the administration had failed to adequately consider the deal’s legal obstacles and strategic implications. Howard speculated that the decision had been made by a small group of advisers without broader consultation across the administration. The potential consequences extend beyond the immediate shipments. Banks and other intermediaries may be wary of congressional subpoenas, requests to testify or future legal challenges, even if they believe a transaction is permitted under the Treasury license. Rachel Ziemba, a senior fellow at the Center for a New American Security, said the warnings reinforced her view that most Russian diesel cargoes would be sold outside the United States. “These warnings reinforce my view that most of any Russian diesel cargos will go to countries outside the US and that it is mostly diplomatic theater,” Ziemba told RFE/RL. She said a meaningful increase in diesel supplies would likely require an energy cease-fire, which she said Russia was wary of agreeing to. The Faces Of Serbia's Student-Backed Political Movement The Students' List, a political grouping of 250 representatives that just won Serbia’s parliamentary elections, has deliberately avoided having a clear leader. While it remains uncertain who Serbia’s prime minister will be, here are some of the high-profile Serbians representing the movement. October 26, 2026 16:37 CET By Amos Chapple and RFE/RL's Balkan Service Who's In Charge? The Faces Of Serbia's Student-Backed Political Movement Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google The Students' List, a political grouping of 250 representatives that just won Serbia’s parliamentary elections, has deliberately avoided having a clear leader. While it remains uncertain who Serbia’s prime minister will be, here are some of the high-profile Serbians representing the movement. Dejan Soskic Dejan Soskic is an economist who served as the governor of the National Bank of Serbia from 2010-2012 and is one of the few list members with high profile government experience. He has frequently called out corruption in the country since resigning from the National Bank, an issue he has claimed is “much more prevalent [in Serbia] than in neighboring countries.” The 59-year-old has vowed a Students' List administration will fire “bad staff” from government positions and launch investigations into ownership of property held by public officials. Additionally, he vowed the list will accelerate reforms needed for Serbia's membership in the European Union, while the final decision on accession would be made through a referendum. Soskic has criticized Western sanctions against Russia and called for a revised approach from Brussels towards the Kremlin. Ilija Srdanovic Ilija Srdanovic is a cardiologist and professor at the University of Novi Sad. The 56-year-old was named the lead candidate for the Students' List in September. Srdanovic has not ruled out taking the prime ministership but said the list has “more than one candidate for every position.” Srdanovic has said the political grouping will prioritize tackling “organized crime and corruption.” He has supported Serbia’s claims on Kosovo, and said a decision on potential Serbian EU accession, “will be made by the citizens.” Dejan Bodiroga Dejan Bodiroga, a former basketball star, currently serves as the president of the Spanish-headquarted Euroleague Basketball. Serbian media have called the 53-year-old the list’s “most famous name,” though his political positions are unclear. He condemned the government’s treatment of student protesters and its portrayal of them as "terrorists.” During protest rallies he called for the protesters to “fight for freedom, for dignity, for a society in which there will be no hatred or division, but mutual respect, justice and solidarity.” Estela Radonjic Zivkov Estela Radonjic Zivkov is a cultural heritage expert who became one of the key figures in the scandal that erupted over plans for a Trump-branded hotel to be built on the site of Belgrade’s NATO-damaged General Staff building. In her position as deputy director of Serbia’s Republic Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments, Zivkov accused the government of violating the law on cultural heritage to greenlight the project. She was later relieved of her deputy director position. She has said that her priority for a Students' List government will be to “restore independence and professional integrity to protection institutions,” and ensure experts can make decisions “based solely on the law and rules of the profession, without political and economic pressure.” Zoran Djajic Engineer Zoran Djajic was among the first to publicly blame corruption for the fatal collapse of the canopy of the Novi Sad railway station. During his own work at the site as a stonework consultant -- which ended in 2023 -- he photographed and reported on what he believed was dangerously poor construction. The 71-year-old has voiced lurid criticism of former Serbian leader Aleksandar Vucic, and was arrested in April 2025 after calling for people to vote for the death penalty for the then president. After the Students' List electoral victory he vowed Vucic would face charges of high treason and wrote that "the time of truth and justice is coming!" Tihomir Stanic Tihomir Stanic is an actor born in today’s Bosnia-Herzegovina who has featured in more than 130 film and television productions. In October 2025, the 65-year old resigned from Belgrade’s Academy of Arts, along with several others over what they described as “gross violation of academic practice and integrity that culminated in threats to students." The veteran actor has called for politics to be excised from Serbia’s cultural institutions, and has claimed the Vucic government “began to determine who would manage the theater, how it would function, who would work, who would not, who would get a chance and who would be punished.” Who's In Charge? By Rikard Jozwiak October 27, 2026 11:55 CET Wider Europe Briefing: Can The EU Put Russia's GRU On Its Terror List? Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Two GRU officers (not pictured) were named as responsible for the Vrbetice ammunition depot explosions in 2014. Welcome to Wider Europe, RFE/RL's newsletter focusing on the key issues concerning the European Union, NATO, and other institutions and their relationships with the Western Balkans and Europe's Eastern neighborhoods. I'm RFE/RL's Europe Editor Rikard Jozwiak, and this week I'm drilling down on two issues: Can the EU add Russia's GRU to its terror list? Plus, more rolling EU sanctions on Moscow. Embed share Wider Europe Briefing: Can The EU Put Russia's GRU On Its Terror List? by RFE/RL Embed share The code has been copied to your clipboard. The URL has been copied to your clipboard No media source currently available 0:00 0:10:55 0:00 Direct link 128 kbps | MP3 64 kbps | MP3 Pop-out player Briefing #1: Can The EU Add The GRU To Its Terror List? What You Need To Know: The European Union is at an early stage of exploring whether it is possible to put the GRU, Russia’s military intelligence agency, on the bloc’s terrorist list. The recent spate of hybrid attacks on various EU member states, many of them either directly or indirectly linked to GRU, has prompted diplomats and lawyers in the club to look into first if it is legally possible, and then to explore if there is enough political will around the table in Brussels to do so. The legality of such a move is being carefully studied, as the move by Brussels to terror list Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) in early January was a watershed moment for the EU. Previously, terrorist designations were reserved for clear non-state actors such as Hamas or Al-Qaeda. Listing the IRGC not only opened the possibility of targeting a formal branch of a sovereign state’s military and intelligence apparatus, but also codified the concept of “state-sponsored terrorism” in the EU’s legal framework. The EU designation of an entity or outfit as a terrorist organization must be based on a previous court decision in an EU member state or a trusted third country. In the case of the IRGC, the legal “smoking gun” was the 2023 ruling by the Dusseldorf higher regional court that an attempted arson attack against a synagogue in the nearby German city of Bochum a year earlier had been explicitly planned and carried out by the Iranian organization. Deep Background: The challenge -- and something that is being looked into right now -- is if there is a similar ruling concerning the GRU. And that can prove tricky. So far, individual member states have officially charged GRU officers, often in absentia, under charges such as espionage or attempted murder -- but not terrorism. According to European diplomats that are familiar with the issue, national prosecutors are restricted to the technical definitions of their respective national penal codes. This means traditional criminal or intelligence-related charges but not terrorism. Look, for example, at the 2014 Vrbetice ammunition depot explosions in the Czech Republic. The country’s prosecutors did name two GRU officers as responsible but Czech law does not allow for a full criminal trial or conviction since the suspects remain in Russia. Or the Salisbury, England, Novichok poisoning targeting the former Russian agent Sergei Skripal and his daughter in 2018. Here, GRU agents (incidentally the same as in Vrbetice) were charged in absentia but for attempted murder and the use of chemical weapons -- not terrorism. Drilling Down Perhaps the two most promising openings for pursuing the GRU as a terrorist organization come from Lithuania. In the first case, it involves an incident in 2024 when incendiary devices were supposed to be planted onto cargo planes bound for the United States and Canada but caught fire in warehouses in Germany, Poland, and the United Kingdom. Lithuanian prosecutors charged 15 individuals in 2025 with terrorism, but these people were GRU-recruited operational proxies rather than direct GRU officers. The question for the legal minds in Brussels to ponder is if this link is strong enough. Then there is the ongoing trial in the Baltic state in which six foreign nationals are accused of planning an arson attack in September 2024 targeting a private military supplier in the Lithuanian city of Siauliai that provides support to Ukraine. As in the first case, these people might be just proxies, but the link to GRU is allegedly a strong one, potentially paving the way for a terror designation. Even if there is a clear legal pathway to designate GRU as a terrorist organization on the EU level, the question is if there is political appetite to go that far. Unanimity among the 27 EU member states is needed and some might argue that keeping diplomatic channels of communication open is essential as Moscow might retaliate to such a move by targeting European embassies, missions, or even culture houses still in the country. The fact that the GRU is already sanctioned by the EU and hence has its assets in the bloc frozen and its leadership under visa ban should be sufficient, according to some Brussels officials. But more hawkish member states believe it is not enough. They note that a formal terror listing covers the entire institution, meaning that every single officer is targeted and therefore closes a loophole in which individuals not yet sanctioned could travel into the EU and operate more easily. Another argument put forward as to why the terror listing is necessary is that it opens up the door for European prosecutors and police forces to arrest and convict the local proxy networks, including EU citizens, that tend to carry out hybrid attacks on behalf of the GRU. It would also make it easier to issue EU-wide counterterrorism arrest warrants, as GRU operations would be fully integrated into Europol’s European Counter Terrorism Center (ECTC), and would strengthen cross-border intelligence tracking of the organization’s communications and safe houses within the bloc. Briefing #2: The EU’s Rolling Russia Sanctions Continue What You Need To Know: The European Union appears poised to continue adding to its Russia sanctions. Having seemingly moved away from big sectoral packages, the current method is to add more visa bans and asset freezes on people and companies on a monthly basis. When EU foreign ministers met on October 12, they formally approved the blacklisting of 1,600 new names, largely from the Russian military industry sector, taking the total number of people and entities sanctioned to over 4,600 since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. When the bloc’s foreign ministers meet again on November 16, they hope to add more. A new proposal, seen by RFE/RL, was presented to the 27 member states’ ambassadors in Brussels on October 21.While smaller in scale than the previous blacklisting -- with only 12 individuals and 105 companies proposed so far -- some of the names in the new proposal are of a much higher level. In the previous round, most EU diplomats, when pressed, could not even name a handful of those sanctioned, reflecting their low significance. https://www.fidh.org/en/en/region/europe.body: 26/10/2026 Impact Belarus en fr Switzerland Universal Jurisdiction Impacts ARND WIEGMANN / AFP The Cantonal Court of St. Gallen has convicted former Special Rapid Response Unit (SOBR) member Yuri Harauski of the enforced disappearance of Anatoly Krasouski in Belarus in 1999, overturning his 2023 acquittal on appeal. The court also established his participation in the enforced disappearances of Yuri Zakharenka and Viktar Hanchar, but upheld Harauski’s acquittal for legal reasons. The court reduced Harauski’s sentence from eight to a two-year suspended prison term, considering his confession and public apology to the victims. St. Gallen, Paris, Minsk, Geneva, 26 October 2026. Following an appeal trial held on 22 September 2026, the Court found Yuri Harauski guilty of the enforced disappearance of well-known Belarusian businessman Anatoly Krasouski in 1999. The Court, however, upheld his acquittal in relation to the disappearances of Yury Zakharenka and Viktar Hanchar. The former member of the SOBR was sentenced to two years’ imprisonment, suspended. Today’s conviction marks the first time a member of the Belarusian security apparatus has been convicted abroad for crimes committed as part of the repression under Aliaksandr Lukashenka’s regime and the first time anywhere in the world that a court ruled on crimes committed in Belarus under the principle of universal jurisdiction. The case was also the first in which the crime of enforced disappearance was examined before a Swiss court. The conviction marks a significant step towards accountability for crimes committed under Aliaksandr Lukashenka’s regime and an important development in Switzerland and beyond. " I feel relieved to have received the guilty verdict ", said Valeriya Krasouskaya, daughter of Anatoly Krasousky . " After 27 years, at least one of the numerous persons involved in the abduction and murder of my father is officially recognised guilty. " TRIAL International, the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) and Human Rights Center Viasna, which initiated the proceedings together with relatives of two of the disappeared men in 2021, welcome the conviction as an important step towards accountability. " For years, impunity for crimes committed under Lukashenka’s regime has looked unassailable. This verdict proves it is not — investigators, prosecutors and courts now have a precedent showing that accountability for Belarusian state crimes is achievable ", said Philip Grant, TRIAL International’s Executive Director . The significance of the judgement may extend beyond Harauski’s own case: by establishing criminal responsibility for acts carried out by a member of the SOBR, it could contribute to broader efforts to examine the chain of responsibility behind the enforced disappearances, including the role of those who ordered or directed the crimes. " The conviction of Yuri Harauski for his involvement in the enforced disappearance of Anatoly Krasouski in Belarus is, first and foremost, a victory for his family, who have finally seen justice served after many years of efforts ", said Alexis Deswaef, FIDH President. " We are grateful to the Swiss justice system for demonstrating that this is possible by advancing international justice based on the principles of universal jurisdiction. " " The court’s verdict in the case against Harauski is the first real step toward investigating the politically motivated disappearances of opposition figures in Belarus in 1999 ”, said Valiantsin Stefanovic, human rights defender with Viasna and former FIDH Vice President . " For the entire Belarusian human rights community, this is a very important day — the day on which the first essential step toward establishing the truth and restoring justice was taken. " While commanding the efforts of the Cantonal Court to ensure adequate access to the proceedings for the victims and the public, the three partner organisations reaffirm the crucial importance of a victim-centered approach, including by guaranteeing the right of plaintiffs to be heard and by ensuring complete, adequate and accessible interpretation during the hearing. https://adcmemorial.org/en/news/breaking.body: Facebook Twitter Вконтакте On October 26, 2026, an informal meeting between members of the UN Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) and NGOs that had submitted reports on violations of women’s rights by the Russian Federation took place in Geneva as part of the Committee’s 93rd session. Representatives of the organizations that had prepared alternative reports delivered brief statements. Kateryna Buriakovska spoke on behalf of the Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group and ADC Memorial Brussels. Among the documented crimes committed by the Russian military and occupation authorities, she highlighted attacks on hospitals and maternity wards, enforced disappearances, various forms of violence, including sexual violence, perpetrated in places of detention, and different forms of gender-based coercion and violence under occupation. These violations have been documented across numerous regions of Ukraine, as well as in detention facilities in Russia and Russian-controlled occupied territories, indicating deliberate and systematic actions rather than isolated incidents or unavoidable consequences of war: “I wish to highlight four patterns of violations documented in our submission. First, maternity healthcare. We documented 34 incidents across 13 Ukrainian regions, including attacks involving precision-guided weapons and the forced removal of mothers and newborns from hospitals converted into military facilities. These incidents raise serious concerns about compliance with international humanitarian law, particularly the protection of medical facilities. Second, enforced disappearances. We documented around 60 cases of missing women with indications of Russian involvement, including journalists, activists and healthcare workers. In one case, Russian authorities denied detaining a journalist despite video evidence of her arrest. Third, sexual violence. Our 76 records represent only a fraction of the likely scale. They include rape, forced nudity, invasive searches and threats of sexual violence. We documented recurring patterns of such abuse across Russian detention facilities. Fourth, coercion under occupation. Women face forced passportisation, prosecution for supporting Ukraine, forced displacement and threats involving their children. Our report documents mock execution of woman accompanied by threats to take away children, as well as cases of children transferred to Russia and not returned to their mothers. In our report, we show how these violations, documented across different regions of Ukraine and Russian controlled institutions, point to deliberate and systematic practices rather than isolated incidents or inevitable consequences of war. We urge the Committee to seek answers from Russia concerning these reported violations, to call upon effective investigations, accountability for perpetrators and remedies for victims. Russia’s obligations under CEDAW do not disappear during occupation. Neither should Ukrainian women disappear from international scrutiny.” The report “ Violations of Women’s Rights Committed by the Russian Federation in the Territory of Ukraine (2022–2026)” Oral Statement on the Situation of Indigenous Women Activists Yana Tannagasheva sent a short video statement on behalf of the International Committee of Indigenous Peoples of Russia, INFOE, North Women, and ADC Memorial Brussels. She emphasized that, in addition to the challenges faced by Indigenous communities in Russia—including difficult living conditions, the activities of extractive companies, access to education, and other issues—the most serious problem in recent years has been the persecution of Indigenous activists and organizations, including accusations of “extremism” and “terrorism.” She recalled that Daria Egereva and Natalia Leongardt remain behind bars, facing criminal prosecution for their peaceful work defending the rights of Indigenous Peoples, including at the UN level, and called for their immediate and unconditional release: “Indigenous women and girls in Russia face systemic discrimination, dispossession and increasingly severe repression. Since CEDAW’s 2021 concluding observations, the situation has worsened. Across the North, Siberia and the Far East, extractive industries threaten our ancestral lands, livelihoods and cultural survival. Women defending these rights face intimidation and criminalization. Russia’s war against Ukraine has brought further suffering to Indigenous communities. Women are left grieving husbands, sons and brothers. In 2024, Russian authorities designated independent Indigenous organizations as “extremist” and “terrorist” organizations . On the 17th December 2025, security forces targeted at least 17 Indigenous activists. Two women, Daria Egereva and Natalia Leongardt, were arrested. They remain detained and face up to twenty years in prison for alleged participation in a “terrorist organization”. In our report, we formed a number of questions, and the most urgent question we urge CEDAW to ask Russia: On what grounds are charges brought against peaceful women – Indigenous rights defenders, treating them as terrorists? We demand their immediate and unconditional release. Defending our land is not terrorism. Defending our rights is not a crime.” The report “The situation of women belonging to Indigenous minority peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East of the Russian Federation” During its 93rd session, the UN Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) will draw up a List of Issues to be addressed to the Russian Federation during the review of its State party report at a future session. https://adcmemorial.org/en/publications/.body: Facebook Twitter Вконтакте The report was submitted by the International Committee of Indigenous Peoples of Russia (ICIPR), the Anti-Discrimination Center “Memorial,” the Institute for Ecology and Anthropology of Action (INFOE), and NorthWomen. The authors argue that since the Committee’s previous review of the situation in Russia in 2021, the situation of indigenous women has “sharply worsened.” Among the key problems, they cite the persecution of human rights defenders, the weakening of independent indigenous institutions, the consequences of war and mobilization, women’s limited participation in decision-making, the impact of extractive industries and climate change, and problems with access to traditional lands, healthcare, and education. The authors recall that Daria Egereva, a representative of the Selkup people, has been involved in international advocacy for indigenous peoples’ rights for over 20 years, including through the UNFCCC, LCIPP, EMRIP, and the UN Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues. She was detained shortly after returning from the COP30 climate conference in Belém. Natalia Leonhardt has also been involved in indigenous peoples’ rights advocacy for over 20 years, including human rights education, documenting violations, and building the capacity of activists. Egereva and Leonhardt have been charged under Article 205.5 of the Russian Criminal Code, which carries lengthy prison sentences for participating in the activities of an organization designated as terrorist. The authors of the parallel report link the women’s criminal prosecution to their environmental and human rights activism and propose that CEDAW request an explanation from the Russian authorities for the basis for applying this article to women defending the rights of indigenous peoples. The report also mentions other indigenous women activists and journalists who were subjected to searches and pressure. The authors note that some were forced to leave Russia. Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу PDF VPN-сіз оқу Сайт бұғатталып тұрса да, материалды осы сілтемемен кіріп оқуға болады Google-да басымдық бер Орталық Азиядағы астық нарығы өзгеріске ұшырап жатыр. Өзбекстан бидай өңдеу қуатын арттырып, Ауғанстанның ұн нарығынан Қазақстанды ығыстырып жатқан тұста аймақтағы астық нарығына Ресей келді. Өз бидайын теңіз арқылы экспорттап келген Ресей шектеулерге тап болып, астықтың бір бөлігін Орталық және Оңтүстік Азияға бұра бастады. Азаттық Азия редакциясы Орталық Азия астық нарығындағы өндірушілер әлеуетін талдап, Ресей бидайының қазақстандық астықты алмастыру ықтималдығын сараптады. Аймақтағы астық нарығы қалай жұмыс істейді? Әлемдік бидай нарығы санаулы экспорттаушы елге тәуелді. 2025 жылы әлемде 808,5 млн тонна бидай өндірілсе, соның тек 215 млн тоннасы ғана халықаралық саудаға шығарылған. Орталық Азиядағы негізгі астық өндіруші – Қазақстан. Астық өндірісі әрі экспорты бойынша әлемде 11-орын алатын Қазақстан 2025 жылы 25,9 млн тонна астық жинаған. Оның 19,3 млн тоннасы бидай болған, ал елдің ішіндегі тұтыну көлемі – шамамен 9 млн тонна. Өнімнің елеулі бөлігі бұрыннан сыртқы нарыққа кетеді. 2025/2026 маркетинг жылы Қазақстан бидай экспортында рекорд орнады. Қазақстан астықты алысқа тасымайды. Әдетте оны Өзбекстан, Тәжікстан, Қырғызстан, Түркіменстан және Ауғанстан алады. Елде астықты ірі көлемде теңіз порттары арқылы алыс мемлекеттерге жеткізу қажеттілігі болмады. Дей тұрғанмен, аймақтағы сауда нарығы біртіндеп өзгеріп жатыр. Миллиондаған тонна бидай сатып алатын Өзбекстан өңдеу өнеркәсібіне басымдық берді. Ұнды негізінен көршілерден сатып алатын Ауғанстан өз диірмендерін қалпына келтіріп, жаңасын да соғып жатыр. Орталық Азияның өзге елдерінде де ұн тарту қуаты артып келеді. Сондықтан "Қазақстан өндіреді, көршілер сатып алады" дейтін бұрынғы схема күрделене түсті. Қазақстан бидайы Өзбекстанға сатылып, ол жерде ұнға айналады да, Ауғанстанға жөнелтіледі. Мұндай жағдайда Қазақстан шикізаттан пайда тапқанымен, өндірістің кейінгі тізбектерінен табыс ала алмайды. Ол табыс бидайдан ұн тартатын көрші елде қалады. Бұл – Қазақстан үшін елеулі өзгеріс. Астық экспортының өсуі елдің аймақтық азық-түлік нарығындағы орны нығайып жатыр дегенді білдірмейді. Егер шикізаттың едәуір бөлігі шетелде өңделсе, Қазақстан астық экспортын қаншалық арттырса да, қосымша құннан және түпкі нарықтан қағылып отырады. Мұндай Ауғанстан мысалынан көруге болады. 2023 жылы Қазақстан Ауғанстанға 1,27 миллион тонна бидай ұнын жөнелтті. 2025 жылға қарай экспорт көлемі шамамен 1,05 миллион тоннаға дейін төмендеді. Ал Өзбекстан Ауғанстанға ұн экспортын күрт арттырды: 2025 жылы Өзбекстан барлығы шамамен 1,6 миллион тонна ұн экспорттаса, соның 1,59 миллион тоннасы Ауғанстанға кеткен. Демек, Қазақстан Ауғанстан нарығынан толық айырылған жоқ, бірақ астықты өңдеудің бір бөлігінен қағылды. Қазақстанның сапалы бидайына сұраныс сақталғанымен, ұн өндірісінен түсетін қосылған құн Өзбекстанда қалып отыр. Қазақстан астық одағы Ауғанстанмен саудада Өзбекстанның географиялық артықшылығы бар деп санайды. Оның үстіне Өзбекстанда өндіріс шығыны төмен және салық саясаты ұтымды, дейді одақ өкілдері. Ал Қазақстан ұн өндірушілері Өзбекстан аумағы арқылы тасымалға да шығынданады. Өзбекстанның өзі өңдеуге басымдық бергенімен, әлі де сапалы бидай импортына тәуелді. Аты-жөнін жарияламауды сұраған өзбекстандық кәсіпкер, әрі көлік және логистика саласының қызметкері Азаттық Азияға берген сұхбатында бидай сапасының маңызы жайлы айтты. "Өзбекстанның өз бидайы бар, бірақ оның желімтегі (глютен) төмен. Сол себепті біз сапалы бидайды импорттап, оны жергілікті бидаймен араластырамыз да, нанға қажет ұнның сапасын арттырамыз" дейді ол. ОҚИ ОТЫРЫҢЫЗ Қазақстандық ұн өндірушілер Ресей бидайын алғанды жөн көреді. Неге? Ресей өз бидайына нарық іздеуге көшті 2026 жылы аймақта қалыптасқан сауда жүйесі тағы күрделене түсті: нарыққа тағы бір ойыншы қосылды. Бұған дейін Ресей астығының басым бөлігін Қара теңіз бен оңтүстік порттар арқылы әлдеқайда ірі нарықтарға сататын. Бірақ 2026 жылы бұл бағыт айтарлықтай шектелді. Украиналық дрондар Қара және Азов теңіздеріндегі ресейлік кемелер мен порт инфрақұрылымына бірнеше рет шабуыл жасады. Осыдан кейін ресейлік компаниялар астықтың бір бөлігін Балтық теңізі мен солтүстіктегі порттарға бұра бастады. Алайда Балтық бағытында да шектеулер туындады. Литва Клайпеда портында Ресей мен Беларусь астығын тексеруді күшейтті. Қыркүйекте Ресей астығының транзиті күрт өскен Латвия партиялардың шыққан жерін тексеріп, оларды тасымалдау мен өңдеу тарифтерін көтеру мәселесін талқылай бастады. Ал Эстония қазанның басынан бастап өз аумағы арқылы Ресей мен Беларусь астығын өткізуге тыйым салды. Сөйтіп, Ресейге жаңа порттар ғана емес, астығын құрлық жолдары немесе Каспий теңізі арқылы жеткізуге болатын жаңа нарықтар да қажет болды. Осылайша таңдау Орталық Азияға түсті. "Ресейде астық бар, өнім жақсы шықты, бірақ оны сыртқа шығаруға мүмкіндік беретін логистика жоқ. Мінеки, Ресейде осындай жағдай қалыптасты. Сондықтан олар бидайына жаңа нарықтар мен балама логистикалық бағыттарды жан-жақты іздеп жатыр. Балама нарықтардың бірі – Қазақстан мен Орталық Азия" дейді Қазақстан астық одағының сараптама комитетіне жетекшілік ететін Евгений Карабанов. Аймақтағы кейбір елдерде бұл өзгерістер қазірдің өзінде-ақ байқалып отыр. 2026 жылдың бірінші жартысында Ресей Қырғызстанға бидай жеткізетін негізгі елге айналды: Қырғызстан сол аралықта Қазақстаннан 64,3 тонна алса, Ресейден 220,2 тонна алған. Қазақстан үшін маңызы жоғары Өзбекстан нарығында әзірге Ресейдің үлесі төмен, бірақ қарқындап артып жатыр. Биыл қаңтар-тамыз аралығында Ресей Өзбекстанға 71 мың тоннадан астам бидай экспорттаған. Бұл – былтырғымен салыстырғанда 16 есе көп көрсеткіш. Соның ішінде 65 тонна тамыз айында ғана экспортталған. Өзбекстандық кәсіпкердің айтуынша, бұл әзірге алаңдатарлық жағдай емес. "Сегіз айға шаққандағы 71 мың тонна – Өзбекстан үшін аз көлем. Біз жыл сайын Қазақстаннан миллиондаған тонна бидай аламыз" дейді кәсіпкер. Қазақстан астық одағының дерегінше, қыркүйектің алғашқы онкүндігінде Қазақстан аумағынан Орталық Азияның өзге елдеріне небәрі 30 мың тоннаға жуық Ресей астығы өткен. Салыстыру үшін айтар болсақ, былтыр Қазақстанның Орталық Азия елдеріне және Ауғанстанға ай сайынғы астық экспорты 1-1,1 млн тонна шамасында болған. "Бұл – біздегі көлемнің 10 пайызы ғана немесе тіпті одан да аз. Сол себепті олардың ықпалы айтарлықтай болмайды деп ойлаймын. Алаңдаушылық болған, бірақ әзірге ол расталған жоқ" дейді Карабанов. Алайда Ресейдің қазіргі экспорты әрдайым сол деңгейде қала бермеуі мүмкін. Астық жинау науқаны әлі толық аяқталған жоқ. ОҚИ ОТЫРЫҢЫЗ Украинаның теңіз жолын жапқан Ресей одан тартып алған астықты сата бастады Қыркүйекте Өзбекстанның Сауда-өнеркәсіп палатасы өкілдері мен Ресейдің "Степь" агрохолдингі 2026 жылы Каспий теңізі арқылы 500 мың тонна бидай жеткізу мүмкіндігін талқылады. Бұл үшін Астрахань және Махачкала порттарын пайдалану жоспарланған. Оның үстіне Ресей 2026 жылдың аяғына дейін астық экспортына баж салығын салмайды. Еуразиялық экономикалық одақ (ЕАЭО) елдеріне Ресейдің экспорттық бажы бұрын да қолданылмайтын. Бірақ бұл аталмыш одаққа кірмейтін Өзбекстанға астық экспорттауға әсер етуі ықтимал. Дегенмен Ресейдің ішкі нарығындағы астық бағасының төмен болуы оның Орталық Азиядағы түпкі сатып алушы үшін де арзанырақ болатынын білдірмейді. Бағаға тасымал шығындары, келісімді қаржыландыру және таңдалған бағыт та әсер етеді. Өзбек кәсіпкерінің сөзінше, осы факторлардың есебінен импорттаушы ел үшін Ресей бидайы Қазақстандікінен 25-35 пайызға қымбат болады. "Бірақ ол бидайды кейінірек төлеу мүмкіндігі болғаны үшін алады. Ресей бір немесе үш айдан кейін төлеуді ұсынып отыр. Бұл импорттаушыға астықты бірден кө

Қайғылы жағдай 25 қазан күні Шишли ауданында болған. DHA агенттігінің тергеу органдарына сілтеп таратқан ақпаратына қарағанда, Бекмаханова өзі тұратын алтыншы қабаттағы пәтердің балконынан көрші үйдің шатырына шығып, шатырдың үстінен өтпек болғанда панельдердің бірі сынып кетіп, марқұм қос ғимараттың ортасына құлаған. Оқиға орнына келген дәрігерлер Бекмаханованың қаза тапқанын анықтаған. Тергеу кезінде Қазақстан азаматының оқиға алдында түсірілген суреті шыққан. Ол суретте қыздың шатыр шетінде отырғаны көрінеді. DHA ақпаратына қарағанда, ол суретті сағат 08:12 шамасында пәтердегі 22 жастағы көршісі, Дарья есімді Ресей азаматы түсірген. Тараған алдын ала мәлімет бойынша, Дарья Бекмахановаға шатырда отыру қауіпті екенін ескерткен, бірақ Бекмаханова отыра беретінін айтып, көршісіне ұйықтай бер деген. Дарья көп ұзамай қатты музыкадан оянып кетіп, бөлмеде құрбысы жоқ екенін аңғарғанын, көрші үйдің шатырындағы панель бұзылғанын, жерде Бекмаханова қозғалыссыз жатқанын көргенін айтқан. Тергеушілердің анықтауынша, осы оқиғаға дейін Бекмаханова 35 жастағы Мазхар Т. есімді дүкен иесімен кездесіп жүрген. Ол Бекмаханованың таңғы 05:30-да дүкенге келіп, ол жерден 07:40-та шығып кеткенін айтқан. Түркия агенттігінің дерегінше, Бекмаханова мен оның көршісі Түркияға 8 қыркүйек күні келген. Тергеу аясында полиция прокуратураның бұйрығы бойынша Дарья мен Мазхар Т. Есімді азаматтарды ұстаған. Олардың процессуалдық мәртебесі әзірге белгісіз. Қазаның себептері әлі анықталып жатыр. Әзірге түрік билігі қорытынды шығармады. Қазақстан сыртқы істер министрлігі Бекмаханованың қазасын растады. Стамбұлда 26 жастағы қазақ қызы қаза тапты. Англия ұлттық құрамасының және германиялық "Бавария" футбол клубының шабуылшысы Харри Кейн 2025-2026 жылғы маусымдағы ойыны үшін "Алтын доп" (Ballon d'Or) иегері атанды. Жеңімпаздың есімі 27 қазанға қараған түні жарияланды. Марапаттау рәсімі Лондонда өтті. Харри Кейн – кейінгі 25 жылда осы марапатты алған алғашқы ағылшын футболшысы. Бұған дейін бұл сыйлық 2001 жылы Майк Оуэнге бұйырған. "Айтарға сөзім жоқ. Шараның Лондонда өтіп жатқаны мен үшін жақсы белгі болды. Маған дауыс берген әрбір адамға алғыс айтамын. Биыл таңдау жасауға қиынға соққанын түсінемін" деді ол салтанатты сөзінде. "Осы жерде әлемдік деңгейдегі бірқатар футболшы отыр. Жеңімпаздар мен үміткерлерді құттықтаймын. Сіздер табандылық пен қажырлы еңбектің арқасында қандай жетістікке жетуге болатынын көрсеттіңіздер". "Бавария" клубына 2023 жылы ауысқан Кейн 2025-2026 жылғы маусымда осы клуб үшін барлық жарыста 51 матч өткізіп, 61 гол соққан. Маусым аяғында ол гол саны бойынша Еуропадағы үздік ойыншы болды. Ал ол ойнаған Англия ұлттық құрамасы биылғы Әлем чемпионатында үшінші орын алды. Бұл додада Кейн 6 гол салған. Биыл "Алтын доп" үшін бәсеке жоғары болды және айқын фаворит болмады. Француз футболшысы Килиан Мбаппе Әлем чемпионатында ең көп гол салған ойыншы болса, испаниялық Ламин Ямал өз құрамасымен бірге әлем чемпионы атанды. "Алтын доп" үміткерлері арасында Мбаппен екінші, Ламин Ямал үшінші орыннан табылды. Испания футболшысы Алексия Путельяс әйелдер арасындағы "Алтын допты" алды. Ол да бұл марапатқа үшінші рет ие болып отыр. Ол ойнаған "Барселона" әйелдер клубы бұл маусымда требл, яғни үш жарыста жеңімпаз болды. Биыл шілдеде Путельяс "Лондон Сити Лайонессис" клубына ауысқан. Биыл номинация жеңімпаздары арасында Испания ұлттық құрамасы мен "Барселона" клубының ойыншылары көп болды. Ламин Ямал "Үздік жас ойыншы" атанды. Ол бұл марапатты осымен үшінші жыл қатарынан алып отыр. Бұл марапат 21 жасқа дейінгі футболшыларға беріледі. Әйелдер арасында бұл сыйлық Испания құрамасы мен "Барселона" әйелдер клубының ойыншысы Вики Лопеске берілді. Испания құрамасының бапкері Луис де ла Фуэнте ерлер арасында үздік бапкер, "Барселона" бапкері Пере Ромеу әйелдер футболының үздік бапкері деп танылды. Ерлер арасындағы үздік қақпашы – Унай Симан (Испания құрамасы, "Атлетик Бильбао"), әйелдер арасындағы үздік қақпашы – Ката Коль (Испания құрамасы, "Барселона"). Ерлер футболындағы үздік клуб – ПСЖ, әйелдер футболындағы үздік клуб – "Барселона". "Алтын доп" – France Football журналының жыл сайын берілетін сыйлығы. Бұл марапат маусым ішіндегі үздік ойын үшін беріледі. https://www.azattyq.org/a/wsj-tramp-akim.body: ЖАҢАЛЫҚТАР WSJ: Трамп әкімшілігі Орбанды БҰҰ Бас хатшысы лауазымына ұсынбақ Азаттық радиосы 26 қазан 2026 жыл, 17:57 WSJ: Трамп әкімшілігі Орбанды БҰҰ Бас хатшысы лауазымына ұсынбақ Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу PDF VPN-сіз оқу Сайт бұғатталып тұрса да, материалды осы сілтемемен кіріп оқуға болады Google-да басымдық бер Виктор Орбан АҚШ президенті Дональд Трамптың әкімшілігі Венгрияның бұрынғы премьер-министрі Виктор Орбанды Біріккен Ұлттар Ұйымының Бас хатшысы лауазымына қолдап отыр. Бұл ұсынысқа Ресей мен Қытай да қосылуы мүмкін. Бұл туралы үш елдегі дереккөзге сілтеме жасаған The Wall Street Journal хабарлады. Айта кетейік, материал басылымның "Көзқарас" (Opinion) бөлімінде жарияланған. Басылымның жазуынша, Вашингтон Орбанды сайлауға түсуге шақырған. Орбан шешім қабылдады ма, жоқ па белгісіз. Газеттің дерегіне сенсек, Вашингтонмен бұған дейін болған келіссөздерге қарағанда, Ресей мен Қытай да бұл жоспарды қолдауы мүмкін. Жоспарға сәйкес, Орбан үш елдің ортақ кандидаты болуы тиіс. АҚШ пен тағы бір елдің шенеуніктері басылымға БҰҰ Қауіпсіздік кеңесінде Вашингтон, Мәскеу және Пекин бір нәрсені қаласа, әдетте соған қол жеткізеді деген. WSJ мақаласына Будапешттен де, Вашингтон, Мәскеу және Пекиннен де реакция болған жоқ. БҰҰ-ның қазіргі Бас хатшысы Антониу Гутерриштің өкілеті биыл 31 желтоқсанда аяқталады. Бас хатшыны Қауіпсіздік кеңесінің ұсынысы бойынша БҰҰ Бас ассамблеясы тағайындайды. Ол үшін үміткер кеңестің 15 мүшесінің кемінде тоғызының дауысын алуы және бес тұрақты мүшенің ешқайсысы вето қоймауы керек. Бұған дейін халықаралық БАҚ ресми кандидаттардың ешқайсысы Қауіпсіздік кеңесінің ортақ қолдауын әзірге ала алмай отырғанын, БҰҰ хатшысын таңдау тығырыққа тірелгенін жазған еді. Өткен аптада бәсекеге Біріккен Араб Әмірліктерінің мемлекеттік министрі Лана Заки Нусейбе қосылды. Ол 2013–2024 жылдары БАӘ-нің БҰҰ жанындағы тұрақты өкілі болған. Сайланса, ол ұйым тарихындағы алғашқы әйел бас хатшы және мысырлық Бутрос Бутрос-Галиден кейінгі Таяу Шығыстан шыққан екінші басшы болмақ. 22 қазанда Қазақстан сыртқы істер министрлігі БАӘ-нің бұл бастамасын құптап, Нусейбенің кандидатурасын қолдайтынын мәлімдеді. Министрлік сайлау Қауіпсіздік кеңесінде консенсусқа қол жеткізудегі қиындықтармен қатар жүріп жатқанын атап өтіп, үміткерлер санының артуын сындарлы диалогты жалғастыруға және өзара қолайлы шешім табуға берілген қосымша мүмкіндік деп бағалады. Бұған дейін британдық The Guardian басылымы БҰҰ бас хатшылығына ықтимал бейресми үміткерлер арасында Қазақстан президенті Қасым-Жомарт Тоқаевтың есімін атаған. Тоқаев БҰҰ-дағы лауазымға бару ниеті жоқ екенін бірнеше рет қайталаған. Сарапшылардың пікірінше, негізгі тартыс қазан-қарашадағы жабық дауыс беру кезінде өрбіп, басты үміткер желтоқсанда анықталуы мүмкін.
